Controls.accumulationEscapeTip: Seconds the ball has to escape before it freezes in place.
Controls.spikesTip: Add inward-pointing spikes on the outer wall as obstacles.
Controls.spikeCountTip: Number of spikes evenly distributed around the outer wall.
Controls.spawnCountTip: How many new balls spawn each time one escapes a wall.
Controls.targetCountTip: How many numbered segments to place on the wall.
Controls.randomOrderTip: Shuffle the position of target numbers around the wall.
Controls.colorCountTip: How many distinct colours are used on the wall segments. Fewer colours = easier to match.
Controls.ballSpeedTip: How fast the ball moves. Higher values make the simulation more energetic.
Controls.ballSizeTip: Radius of the ball in pixels. Larger balls have a harder time fitting through gaps.
Controls.gravityTip: Downward pull on the ball. Set to 0 for zero-gravity floating.
Controls.twoBallsTip: Spawn a second ball moving in the opposite direction for double the action.
Controls.bouncierTip: Ball gets faster with every wall bounce, building momentum until it escapes.
Controls.wallCountTip: Number of concentric circular walls the ball must break through.
Controls.wallThicknessTip: Thickness of each wall ring in pixels.
Controls.gapSizeTip: Size of the opening in each wall. Larger gaps make it easier for the ball to escape.
Controls.rotationTip: Walls rotate over time, making the gaps move around the circle.
Controls.trailsTip: Show a fading trail behind the ball as it moves.
Controls.ballGlowTip: Radial light effect around the ball.
Controls.wallGlowTip: Walls flash with colour when the ball bounces off them.
Controls.colorTrailTip: Rainbow hue-shifting trail behind the ball.
Controls.reactiveBgTip: Background pulses and shifts colour on each bounce.
Controls.cameraFollowTip: Smoothly shifts the viewport to keep the ball centred.
Controls.cinematicTip: Subtly steers rebounds to create near-misses and dramatic escapes. Turn off for pure physics.
Controls.trailThicknessTip: How thick the ball's trail is. Higher values create a bolder streak.
Controls.wallBreakEffectTip: Visual effect that plays when the ball breaks through a wall.
Controls.wallBreakSoundDesc: Play a custom audio clip instead of the default tones when the ball breaks through a wall.
Controls.hitSoundModeTip: What plays when the ball bounces off a wall: the synthesised tones (or a melody) or an audio clip of your own.
Controls.hitSampleDesc: Pick a built-in clip or upload your own. It plays on every wall bounce and is included in recordings.
Controls.hitSamplePitchByWallTip: Inner walls play the clip at a higher pitch and outer walls lower, following the same curve as the default tones.
Controls.hitSampleVolumeTip: Loudness of the hit sample relative to the other sounds.
Controls.hitSampleDecodeError: Could not decode this audio file – the synth tones play instead. Try an MP3, OGG, WAV or M4A file.
Controls.customSoundDesc: Choose a song to use its melody as bounce sounds. Each wall hit plays the next note from the song.
Controls.midiSourceText: Not sure where to get MIDI files? Try
Controls.midiParseError: Failed to parse MIDI file. Make sure it is a valid format 0 or 1 MIDI file.
Controls.sliceSongTip: The viral format: upload any song and every bounce plays the next little piece of it, so the ball "plays" the track.
Controls.sliceSongDesc: Upload an MP3, OGG, WAV or M4A file. Each wall hit plays the next slice of the song, continuing from where the last one stopped. The song stays in your browser.
Controls.sliceEnabledTip: While on, slices of the uploaded song replace the bounce tones and melody notes.
Controls.sliceLengthTip: How much of the song each bounce plays. Short slices sound choppy and rhythmic; long ones let whole phrases through.
Controls.sliceLoopTip: Start the song over when it reaches the end. When off, bounces go back to the default tones after the last slice.
Controls.sliceFadeTip: Fade-in and fade-out at the edges of every slice so the cuts don't click.
Controls.sliceDecodeError: Could not decode this audio file. Try an MP3, OGG, WAV or M4A file.
Controls.sliceNoSong: Upload a song to hear it – the default tones play until then.
Controls.musicBedTip: Mixes a music track under the bounce sounds and records it into the exported video, so the clip is ready to post. The file stays in your browser.
Controls.musicBedDesc: Upload an MP3, OGG, WAV or M4A file to play under the bounce sounds. It dips on every hit so the tones stay clear, then swells back. The track stays in your browser.
Controls.musicDecodeError: Could not decode this audio file. Try an MP3, OGG, WAV or M4A file.
Controls.musicVolumeTip: How loud the music plays under the bounce sounds – in the speakers and in the exported video.
Controls.musicDuckingTip: How much the music dips on every bounce and wall break. 0% keeps it steady, 100% mutes it for an instant, like a sidechain compressor.
Controls.musicDuckReleaseTip: How long the music takes to swell back after a bounce, in milliseconds. Short is punchy, long is smooth.
Controls.musicLoopTip: Start the track again when it ends. Off: the music stops at the end of the track and stays silent until the next run.
Controls.musicStartOffsetTip: Skip the first seconds of the track so the drop lands right when the simulation starts. Restarts begin from here too.
Controls.instrumentDesc: The voice the wall tones are played with (a melody picks its own instrument below). Pluck, marimba and chip are synthesised live; the classic tone is Triangle.
Controls.melodyInstrumentDesc: The voice the notes of the chosen song are played with. Sine is the classic melody sound.
Controls.scaleDesc: Snap wall tones and melody notes to the nearest note of a scale so every bounce is in key. Chromatic keeps the original pitches.
Controls.beatLockTip: Delays each bounce sound to the next point of the beat grid (at most one grid step) so exports sit on the beat.
Controls.beatLockDesc: Play bounce sounds on a BPM grid; extra hits inside the same step are skipped so the rhythm stays clean.
Controls.durationTip: The simulation will automatically stop and save after this many seconds.
Controls.watermarkTip: Text displayed faintly in the centre of your exported recording.
Controls.saveHint: Save your current setup (colours, physics, effects) to use later.
Controls.growthRateTip: How fast the ball grows with each bounce (as a percentage).
Controls.centerDotTip: Place a small dot in the centre of the circle that the ball bounces off.
Controls.growLinesTip: Draw lines from each bounce point to the ball, like in Lines mode.
Controls.finderDesc: Find a simulation seed that runs for the exact duration you select, keeping all your custom settings in mind.
Controls.topTextTip: Custom text overlay displayed above the physics arena.
Controls.bottomTextTip: Custom text overlay displayed below the physics arena.
Controls.textSizeTip: Adjust the font size of the text overlays.
Controls.findSimulationTip: Search for a simulation seed that produces a run of the exact target duration.

classic.name: Classic
classic.description: A ball bounces inside concentric rings that each have a single gap. Every wall it slips through breaks with a satisfying effect. Simple, hypnotic and endlessly rewatchable.

accumulation.name: Accumulation
accumulation.description: The ball has a few seconds to escape before it freezes where it is. Every frozen ball becomes an obstacle for the next one. Will the last ball make it out?

multiply.name: Multiply
multiply.description: Each time a ball escapes the ring it spawns extra balls. The arena fills with bouncing chaos within seconds, which makes for explosive, shareable clips.

lines.name: Lines
lines.description: Every bounce point is connected to the ball by a line, so the run slowly draws intricate string art as the ball ricochets around the circle.

paint.name: Paint
paint.description: The ball paints a rainbow trail wherever it goes, gradually colouring the whole circle while a live percentage counter tracks the coverage.

target.name: Target
target.description: Numbered segments line the wall and must be hit in order. Every correct hit triggers a wall-break effect; wrong hits flash red.

grow.name: Grow
grow.description: The ball is sealed inside one large ring and grows a little with every bounce, filling more and more of the space until there is nowhere left to go.

shatter.name: Shatter
shatter.description: Every wall is made of segments with hit points. Each bounce cracks a segment and enough hits shatter it. Clear a path through every wall to escape.

colorMatch.name: Color Match
colorMatch.description: The wall is split into coloured segments and the ball changes colour on every bounce. A segment only breaks when the colours match. Clear them all to escape.

portal.name: Portal
portal.description: Colour-matched portal pairs sit on the wall. Touch one and the ball teleports to its twin. After enough uses the portals burn out and become exits.

wallBreak.name: Wall Break Effects
wallBreak.description: Confetti, glass shatter, a shockwave, all three at once, or none. Every time the ball breaks through a wall, your chosen effect plays.

rainbowWalls.name: Rainbow Walls
rainbowWalls.description: Walls cycle through the spectrum in two styles: a smooth gradient across all rings, or a reactive pulse that flashes colour on every hit.

glow.name: Ball & Wall Glow
glow.description: Toggle a soft radial glow around the ball and a flash on the walls independently, so you get exactly the amount of shine you want.

colorTrail.name: Colour Trail
colorTrail.description: The ball leaves a vivid, hue-shifting streak behind it, so fast motion reads as intentional rather than messy.

reactiveBg.name: Reactive Background
reactiveBg.description: The backdrop pulses and shifts colour with every bounce, making each hit feel heavier.

bouncier.name: Increasing Bounciness
bouncier.description: The ball speeds up with every wall hit until it finally breaks free, then the boost resets for the next ring.

customBall.name: Custom Ball Image
customBall.description: Replace the ball with your own image or an emoji: a logo, a face, a product. It scales and moves with the ball.

textOverlays.name: Text Overlays
textOverlays.description: Add a top and a bottom caption with adjustable size for hooks, branding or calls to action, baked into the export.

spikes.name: Spikes
spikes.description: Add inward-pointing spikes to the outer wall that freeze the ball on contact, raising the stakes in Accumulation mode.

videoExport.name: Video Export
videoExport.description: Record the run as an MP4 in square, HD, Full HD or vertical TikTok (1080×1920) format, from 10 to 120 seconds long.

savePresets.name: Save & Load Presets
savePresets.description: Store the whole configuration, mode, colours, physics and effects, in your browser and load it back with one click.

watermark.name: Custom Watermark
watermark.description: Stamp your handle faintly in the centre of the ring so reposts still credit you.

customSound.name: Custom Sound
customSound.description: Pick a melody from the built-in library or import your own MIDI file, and every wall hit plays the next note. Play an audio clip – built-in or uploaded – on every bounce instead, or upload a whole song and let each bounce play its next slice. Choose one of seven instruments, snap every bounce to a musical scale and lock the sounds to a BPM grid.

q1.question: Is {siteName} free to use?
q1.answer: Yes. The simulator, every mode, every customisation option and the video export are free, and there is no account to create.

q2.question: What video formats and resolutions can I export?
q2.answer: You can record 500×500 (square), 1280×720 (HD), 1920×1080 (Full HD) and 1080×1920 (vertical, TikTok) clips between 10 and 120 seconds long. Browsers that support MP4 recording export MP4; others export WebM.

q3.question: Can I use the exported videos commercially?
q3.answer: Yes. Everything you create is yours to use on TikTok, YouTube, Instagram or anywhere else, with no attribution required.

q4.question: Do I need to install anything?
q4.answer: No. The whole tool runs in your browser. Open the site and start creating.

q5.question: Can I save my settings?
q5.answer: Yes. Save as many presets as you like to your browser's local storage and load them back at any time. The URL also updates as you tweak settings, so you can bookmark or share a setup.

q6.question: Does it work on mobile?
q6.answer: The simulator is designed for desktop browsers, where there is room for the canvas and the controls side by side. It runs on phones too, but a laptop or desktop is the better experience.

q7.question: Are there keyboard shortcuts?
q7.answer: Yes. Press Space to pause or resume and R to restart the simulation.

q8.question: How do I upload a custom ball image?
q8.answer: Open the Ball & Physics section, enable Show Advanced Options and click Choose Image. Any image works: logos, photos, memes. Or pick an emoji from the emoji grid.

q9.question: How does the custom sound feature work?
q9.answer: In the Custom Sound section, choose a song from the built-in library or import a MIDI file. The melody is extracted from the file and every wall hit plays its next note, turning the run into a musical performance. Prefer a sound effect? Switch Bounce Sound to Audio sample and pick a built-in click, pluck or kick, or upload your own clip – it is pitched per wall and included in the recording.

q10.question: What makes {siteName} a satisfying ball simulator?
q10.answer: The loop is simple: a ball bounces inside rings with tiny gaps, and every time it slips through something rewarding happens: confetti, a shatter, a shockwave. Because you control physics, colours and effects, the tension and the payoff look exactly the way you want.

q11.question: Can I use {siteName} as a satisfying ball clicker?
q11.answer: It is not a clicker game, but it scratches the same itch. You watch, anticipate the gap and get rewarded with effects and sound on every escape. The run plays itself, so it is the satisfaction without the tapping.

AboutTool.title: What {siteName} actually is
AboutTool.p1: {siteName} is a browser tool for making the bouncing-ball videos that fill TikTok, Reels and YouTube Shorts. Pick a mode, adjust a few settings, press record and download the clip. There is no account, no installation and no video editor involved; everything happens in the tab you already have open, so an idea becomes a finished video in a couple of minutes.
AboutTool.p2: The format works because it is simple. A ball bounces inside a ring with a gap. Every time it slips through, something pays off: a wall shatters, the ball multiplies, colour floods the screen, a target is hit. Viewers want to know how it ends, so they keep watching. That small loop of tension and release is what drives the views, and here you control every part of it instead of reposting someone else's clip.
AboutTool.p3: Each of the ten modes tells a different kind of story. Classic is the one most people picture: a ball breaking out through rings. Multiply turns one ball into a swarm. Accumulation freezes balls in place until the last one has to thread a maze of its predecessors. Paint, Target, Grow, Shatter, Color Match, Lines and Portal each change the rules in their own way. Switching takes one click and the canvas updates immediately.
AboutTool.p4: The look is yours. Add rings for a longer build-up or remove them for a fast payoff. Turn on rainbow walls, switch the break effect between confetti, shatter and shockwave, or stack all three. Add spikes for danger, glow for polish and a colour trail so fast motion looks deliberate. Put your own image on the ball, write a hook like "will it escape?" across the top and load a melody so the bounces land on a beat. Small changes matter: one extra ring can be the difference between a clip people skip and one they watch twice.
AboutTool.p5: When the run looks right, record it in the browser and export a video sized for vertical feeds. No screen-capture app, no unwanted watermark, no re-encoding elsewhere. Found a combination you like? Save it as a preset and reuse it for a whole series; many accounts post the same mode every day with small variations.
AboutTool.p6: Reposting a clip that a hundred other accounts already used gives the algorithm, and your audience, nothing new. When you build the run yourself you decide the hook, the colours, the pacing and the moment it pays off. You can match a trending sound, add your handle and post a fresh version every day without repeating yourself, and original content never trips the reused-content filters that quietly limit reach.
AboutTool.p7: The defaults already produce a clip worth posting. From there, change one thing at a time and watch what happens: add a ring, swap the break effect, turn the glow up. Because the canvas reacts immediately you learn what each setting does by using it, and after a few sessions you develop a feel for which combinations land.
AboutTool.p8: Most people here are creators chasing reach without a budget: no camera, no studio, no design background, just a hook and a few minutes of tuning. Teachers use it to show motion and collisions in a way students actually watch. Plenty of people open it just to play, because a ball smashing through rings is fun on its own. The controls are the same for everyone.
AboutTool.p9_before: {siteName} is free. Presets and settings live in your own browser, videos render on your own machine and there is no sign-up wall. If you want to go deeper on a mode or find settings that tend to perform, the
AboutTool.p9_mid: breaks each one down with examples, and if something feels off or you wish a setting existed, the
AboutTool.p9_after: goes straight to the person building it.

Instructions.title: Every control, explained
Instructions.description: This is the simulator layout: a live canvas on the left and the controls panel on the right. The numbers on the mockup match the steps beside it.
Instructions.mockupCaption: A simplified view of the simulator screen.

step1.title: Pick a mode
step1.body: Open the Mode row in the controls panel and choose one of the ten modes. The mode sets the rules, so decide it first.

step2.title: Open a section and tweak it
step2.body: Ball, Wall, Visual and Sound each expand when clicked. Change the wall count, the break effect, the colours or the trail. In a hurry? Type a setting name into the search box at the top.

step3.title: Press Start
step3.body: Hit Start simulator on the canvas. The defaults already look good, so start right away and adjust once you see it move.

step4.title: Get the run right
step4.body: While it plays, use Restart to reroll, Pause to hold a frame and the speed buttons (1x to 8x) to skip ahead. Space pauses, R restarts. Reset until the timing lands the way you want.

step5.title: Set length and size
step5.body: Open the Recording section to choose how long the clip runs and its resolution. 1080×1920 is the vertical size for TikTok, Reels and Shorts.

step6.title: Record, and it downloads
step6.body: Press Record video. It captures the run with sound and saves the file to your device. Like the setup? Save it as a preset and reuse it for a whole series.

Editorial.physicsP1: Every run starts from the same idea: a ball bouncing inside a ring. Speed, gravity and bounciness change how it moves, a bit like dropping a real ball into a bowl and deciding how fast it falls and how hard it ricochets. The engine steps the world sixty times per second with several sub-steps per frame, so collisions stay stable even at high speed.
Editorial.physicsP2: Each ring has a small gap. When the ball lines up with it and passes through, the ring breaks with the effect you picked: confetti, shattering glass or a shockwave. The ball moves on to the next ring, and the process repeats until it escapes or the recording ends.
Editorial.physicsP3: Every mode layers its own rules on top: the ball might split into a swarm, freeze into an obstacle course, or grow with every bounce. All of it runs locally in your browser; nothing is uploaded and the video is encoded on your own machine.
Editorial.modeClassic: A single ball bounces through concentric rings, each with a gap. Break through every wall to escape. The default mode: simple, hypnotic and endlessly watchable.
Editorial.modeAccumulation: The ball has limited time to escape. If it fails, it freezes in place and becomes a new obstacle, and a fresh ball spawns. The arena fills up fast. Can the last one get out?
Editorial.modeMultiply: Each time a ball escapes the ring it spawns extra balls, so one ball quickly becomes a swarm. Great for explosive, chaotic clips that fill the screen.
Editorial.modeLines: Every bounce point is connected to the ball by a line, producing intricate geometric patterns. Part physics, part generative art.
Editorial.modePaint: The ball leaves a colourful trail as it moves, gradually covering the circle. A percentage counter tracks how much you have painted. Try to reach 100%.
Editorial.modeTarget: Numbered segments appear on the wall. Hit them in order; each correct hit triggers a break effect, and wrong hits flash red.
Editorial.modePortal: Colour-matched portal pairs sit on the wall. Touch one to teleport to its twin. After enough uses the portals burn out and the ball breaks free.
Editorial.modeShatter: Walls are split into segments with hit points. Each bounce cracks a segment and after enough hits it shatters. Clear a path through all walls to escape.
Editorial.modeColorMatch: The wall is split into coloured segments and the ball changes colour on every bounce. A segment breaks only when the colours match. Clear them all to win.
Editorial.modeGrow: The ball is sealed inside a single ring and grows with every bounce, taking up more and more of the space until it can barely move.
Editorial.tipFindSimulationBody: Rather than guessing, let the tool search for a seed that produces a run of your target length. Open Find Simulation below the canvas, set the duration and let it scan seeds. Once it finds one, the run lasts exactly that long, which makes recording predictable.
Editorial.tipLayerEffectsBody: Rainbow walls, glow, colour trails and wall-break effects stack. Try a reactive background with confetti breaks and a glow; the extra layers keep viewers watching.
Editorial.tipTextHooksBody: Top and bottom overlays give context. A question like "Will it escape?" or a countdown builds anticipation. Adjust the text size so it is readable at a glance on a phone.
Editorial.tipClipLengthTitle: Match the clip length to the platform
Editorial.tipClipLengthBody: Shorter clips (15 to 30 seconds) tend to perform better on TikTok and Reels. Set the duration in the Recording section and pick the vertical 1080×1920 resolution.
Editorial.tipPresetsTitle: Save your favourite setups as presets
Editorial.tipPresetsBody: When a configuration works, save it and load it again for your next video. Consistent series perform well because the audience knows what to expect.
Editorial.tipSpeedBody: Use the 2× to 8× speed buttons to fast-forward through a long run while previewing. Before recording, set it back to 1× so the export captures every frame at full quality.
Editorial.troubleExportQ: The video export looks wrong or is missing frames
Editorial.troubleExportA: Use a recent version of Chrome, Edge or Firefox; recording works best there. Close other tabs and apps to free up memory, and keep the simulator tab visible while it records. Chrome and Safari export MP4; Firefox exports WebM, which every major platform accepts.
Editorial.troubleAudioQ: The simulation does not play audio
Editorial.troubleAudioA: Browsers block sound until you interact with the page. Click anywhere first, then press Start. If there is still no sound, check the system volume and make sure the site is allowed to play audio.
Editorial.troubleSpeedQ: The ball moves too fast or too slow
Editorial.troubleSpeedA: Open the Ball & Physics section and adjust Ball Speed. Lower values are easier to follow; higher values give more energetic clips. Gravity also changes the pacing: lower gravity keeps the ball floating longer between hits.
Editorial.troubleSettingsA: Presets are stored in your browser's local storage. Clearing site data or using a private window removes them. Copy the share link of a setup you care about so you can restore it later.
Editorial.troubleMidiQ: My custom MIDI file does not load
Editorial.troubleMidiA: Very complex files with many simultaneous tracks may not parse. Try a simpler single-melody MIDI (format 0 or 1). The tool keeps only the highest note at each moment, so a lead-melody export from your music software works best.
Editorial.troubleStuckA: Send a note through the feedback page and describe what you were doing.

introduction.title: 1. Introduction
introduction.content: Welcome to {siteDomain} ("we", "our", "us"). We respect your privacy and keep the amount of information connected to your use of this site as small as possible. This policy explains what is collected, how it is used and what your rights are.

information.title: 2. Information We Collect
information.subtitle: We collect the minimum needed to run and improve the service:

analytics.label: Analytics data:
analytics.content: If analytics are enabled, we use a privacy-focused service that records anonymous usage statistics such as page views, browser type, screen size and approximate region. It does not identify you personally.

localStorage.label: Local storage data:
localStorage.content: Your simulator settings and presets are stored in your browser's local storage. They never leave your device and are not sent to our servers.

images.label: Uploaded images and audio:
images.content: Custom ball images, MIDI files and sound clips are processed entirely in your browser. Nothing is uploaded, stored or transmitted.

TikTokBallVideos.metaTitle: Make Bouncing Ball Videos for TikTok – Free Tool – {siteName}
TikTokBallVideos.metaDescription: Create hypnotic bouncing-ball videos for TikTok with {siteName}: a free browser tool with 10 modes, custom physics and vertical 1080×1920 export. No sign-up needed.
TikTokBallVideos.title: Bouncing Ball Videos for TikTok
TikTokBallVideos.p1: Bouncing-ball simulations are one of the most dependable formats on TikTok. The premise is tiny, a ball trapped inside rings with narrow gaps trying to bounce its way out, but the payoff is satisfying enough to hold attention for a whole short-form clip. {siteName} is a free browser tool built for exactly this kind of content, with physics controls, visual effects and one-click vertical export.
TikTokBallVideos.p2: What makes the format work is its built-in tension arc. The ball ricochets faster, the walls close in, the gap looks impossibly small, and then the ball slips through and everything pays off with confetti, a shatter or a shockwave. That loop fits naturally into 15 to 60 seconds, which is where TikTok engagement peaks.
TikTokBallVideos.p3: TikTok rewards videos that hold viewers to the end and get replayed. Ball physics does both: people stay to see whether the ball escapes and rewatch to catch the effects they missed. The format also fits TikTok's sound culture: {siteName} can play a melody note by note on every wall hit, turning the physics into a musical performance.
TikTokBallVideos.p4: There is no dialogue, no face on screen and no setup. Just a clean visual hook that works even as background noise for a scrolling viewer, which is why the format regularly out-performs more produced content in the discovery feed.
TikTokBallVideos.p5: TikTok's preferred aspect ratio is 9:16 vertical, 1080×1920 pixels. {siteName} records directly at that size, so there is no cropping, no re-encoding and no external editor. Set the recording duration (10 to 120 seconds), press record and download a platform-ready clip.
TikTokBallVideos.p6: You can also export 500×500 (square), 1280×720 (HD) or 1920×1080 (Full HD) for Reels, YouTube Shorts and other platforms. Recording happens entirely in your browser; nothing is uploaded and no watermark is added unless you add your own.
TikTokBallVideos.p7: The best TikTok ball videos follow a simple recipe: a clear visual hook in the first second, a visible progress indicator such as the number of walls left, and a satisfying payoff when the ball finally escapes. The Find Simulation tool searches for a seed that produces a run of your target length, so you can plan the clip instead of guessing.
TikTokBallVideos.p8: All ten modes, Classic, Accumulation, Multiply, Lines, Paint, Target, Grow, Shatter, Color Match and Portal, produce a different rhythm, so you can vary your content without starting over. Save your favourite setups as presets and post a new video every day with one click.

About.metaTitle: About {siteName} – Free Ball Physics Video Maker
About.metaDescription: The story behind {siteName}: a free, browser-based tool for making the bouncing-ball videos that go viral on TikTok, Reels and YouTube Shorts.
About.metaOgDescription: Why {siteName} exists and who it is for.
About.title: About {siteName}
About.p1: {siteName} started with a simple frustration. Bouncing-ball physics videos were everywhere, pulling in millions of views, and every way of making one was clunky: learn a game engine, pay for an app, or repost a clip a thousand other accounts had already used. None of that suited someone who just wanted to make a good video and post it. So we built the tool we wished existed: open a tab, make the video, download it, done.
About.p2: That idea still runs the whole site. {siteName} is free, works in your browser and asks nothing of you before you start. No sign-up, no install, no paywall between you and a finished clip. The defaults already produce something worth posting; everything after that is you shaping it to fit your idea.
About.p3: Speed and control, more than anything else. Speed, because the gap between an idea and a posted video is where most content dies; if a clip takes twenty minutes and three apps, you stop making clips. Control, because reposted content does not grow an account. When you set the mode, the colours, the pacing and the hook yourself, the video is yours and it stands a real chance in a feed that has seen every recycled clip.
About.p4: We also care about staying out of your way. The simulator updates as you change things, so you learn by doing rather than reading a manual. Settings have plain names. The hard part, the physics and the rendering, happens quietly in the background while you focus on whether the video is fun to watch.
About.p5: Your work stays with you. Presets and settings live in your browser and videos render on your own machine, not on a server we control. We are not interested in harvesting your data or locking your creations behind an account. The less we know about you, the better the tool feels to use. The details are in our <privacy>privacy policy</privacy>.
About.p6: {siteName} is a small, independent project rather than a venture-backed company with a roadmap full of upsells, and that shapes what gets built. New modes and settings appear because creators ask for them. When you write in through the <feedback>feedback page</feedback>, the note reaches the person actually working on the tool, and a lot of what is in the simulator today exists because someone asked for it.
About.p7: The plan is to keep the core free and keep adding modes, effects and quality-of-life touches that make a good clip faster to build. On the <blog>blog</blog> we break down which settings tend to perform and why certain videos hook people, so the tool and the knowledge around it grow together. If you make something with it, that is the whole point. Go make a ball smash through some walls.
